answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning power to verified, non-transferable work history rather than account count: each identity must complete small, peer-checked tasks over time before it can claim larger rewards, and its reputation decays if it goes idle or is caught copying. A dune looks solid from afar but shifts under weight, and the same test applies here — a hollow identity with no track record cannot stand on the same ledge as a proven worker, because only reputation built slowly unlocks real payouts, so thousands of fresh shells buy no advantage.
